headline: AMD chief executive Lisa Su held a long dinner meeting with Samsung's chip chief in Seoul and gave no details of a foundry deal.
score_reason: Pool 5 kept: one outlet reports the meeting and quotes; no deal announced.
importance_line: What changed: AMD and Samsung are still talking about memory supply and chip making, which matters to AMD's AI chip customers and to Samsung's chip business; Chosun's reading that AMD needs memory while Samsung wants chip orders is an industry interpretation, and no new deal was announced.
summary: Chosun Biz reports that AMD chief executive Lisa Su met Jun Young-hyun, vice chair of Samsung Electronics and head of its chip division, for a little over three hours, including dinner, in Seoul on 7 Oct, following our 7 Oct report from the Korea Herald that she is courting Korean AI chipmakers. Lisa Su, AMD's chief executive, called the partnership 'very broad' without detailing progress on foundry (contract chip making), and the March memorandum covers AMD's supply of HBM4 memory and server DRAM, with producing AMD's next-generation products at Samsung's foundry still to be discussed.
